title: Diffusion Models
interviewAnswer: Diffusion models learn to reverse a progressive corruption process. During generation they start from noise and iteratively move toward a sample from the learned data distribution.
why: Diffusion appears frequently in modern image generation and connects naturally to denoising, score/velocity prediction and latent models.
intuition: Training creates noisy versions of real data and teaches the model how to move them toward clean data. At inference, start from noise and repeatedly apply the learned reverse dynamics.
deepDive: Different formulations predict noise ε, clean data x₀, velocity v or a score. The forward corruption process is known, while the neural network approximates the reverse process. Latent diffusion runs this process in a compressed representation to reduce compute.
math: One common forward form: xₜ = √ᾱₜ x₀ + √(1-ᾱₜ) ε,  ε~N(0,I)
code:
# Pseudocode
for x0 in data:
    t = sample_timestep()
    eps = randn_like(x0)
    xt = add_noise(x0, eps, t)
    pred = model(xt, t, condition)
    loss = mse(pred, eps)
commonMistakes: “Diffusion just removes Gaussian noise.” It learns conditional reverse dynamics across noise levels.
Assuming lower pixel MSE always means better generative quality.
production: Sampling latency can be significant because inference uses multiple model evaluations; distillation, better solvers and latent-space models reduce cost.
workedExample: A conditioned reconstruction model can start from noise and use a compact semantic representation to guide the reverse process toward a compatible microstructure.

lab.goal: Train intuition with the forward noising equation and a tiny denoising target.
lab.buildIt:
import torch
x0=torch.randn(8,3,32,32); eps=torch.randn_like(x0)
alpha_bar=torch.tensor(.6)
xt=alpha_bar.sqrt()*x0+(1-alpha_bar).sqrt()*eps
# A diffusion network would receive (xt,t,condition) and predict eps/v/x0.
print(x0.std().item(),xt.std().item())

visual.caption: Training learns the reverse of a gradual corruption process; sampling repeatedly removes noise from an initial random state.
